title: Mike Evans injury update: WR avoids long-term Achilles injury, but how will 49ers fare if he misses time? - CBS Sports
description: The 49ers' offense struggled mightily in Evans' second-half absence against the Commanders
body:
The 49ers' offense struggled mightily in Evans' second-half absence against the Commanders
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:12 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The San Francisco 49ers had to finish their 23-17 "Monday Night Football" win over the Washington Commanders without their top receiver, as Mike Evans left the game just ahead of halftime with an Achilles tendon injury. While the 49ers held onto their lead and closed out the victory without him, Evans' absence was noticeable as the offense scored just three points in the final two quarters. Fortunately for San Francisco, Evans may not miss much additional time.Coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Evans experienced a flare-up of the Achilles tendinitis that bothered him throughout the week and that he will not undergo further testing."It's something that he's had before, something that bothered him throughout the week," Shanahan said. "When you have Achilles tendinitis like he does, it kind of is what it is. It flared up tonight, and I hope he recovers throughout the week. You don't think it's a long-term thing, but right now it almost cost him this game and ended up costing him two quarters. "Hopefully he'll be able to play next week, but if not, we'll have to have the rest of the group step up, and hopefully we can get him healed up by after the bye week."
It was a close call on whether Evans would suit up in Week 6 in the first place. He did not practice leading up to the game, and Shanahan noted that even though he declared himself healthy enough to play, there was always a chance that Evans would not be able to remain on the field for all four quarters.Evans was seen during the game stretching his Achilles tendon. The flare-up occurred thereafter when he made a catch late in the second quarter. He immediately went into the locker room, and television broadcast cameras captured him grabbing at his Achilles in the tunnel.The undefeated 49ers hit the road in Week 7 for a matchup against the Atlanta Falcons and will be idle the following week. They return from their bye in Week 9 for a home date with the Las Vegas Raiders.
49ers offense could be in trouble without Mike EvansIf the tendinitis forces Evans to miss Sunday's game in Atlanta, the 49ers and their top-three scoring offense could have a difficult time moving the ball. The contrast in production with Evans in and out of the lineup against the Commanders was stark. He caught three passes for a game-high 94 yards in the first half as San Francisco rolled to a 20-3 lead, but the team managed just three points in the second half and nearly blew the three-score advantage.Evans paces the 49ers in targets and receiving yards in his first year with the team and ranks 13th in the NFL in yards and sixth in touchdowns. He has been among the league's most prolific free agency signings from the 2026 offseason.Shanahan chalked up the second-half struggles to sacks and a general lack of offensive execution, but it is difficult to imagine the 49ers would not have found it easier to move the ball if their top wide receiver was still on the field.
"It's definitely a big deal when you lose a player like Mike," Shanahan said. "Just the way it ended up being, Mike wouldn't have had a chance to have much of an effect there in the second half. Now, if we would've gotten some first downs and stuff and got driving, we would've felt the lack of presence of him, but we didn't get enough first downs to show where we would miss him."Wide receiver injuries decimated the San Francisco offense over the season's first month and a half. While Shanahan said there is a possibility Christian Kirk will return from injured reserve for Week 7, it is not a guarantee. He also noted that Demarcus Robinson is unlikely to return for the trip to Atlanta.49ers wide receiver injuriesMike Evans, Achilles: Missed second half in Week 6Deebo Samuel, hamstring: Missed Week 6, expected to miss multiple gamesChristian Kirk, calf: Injured reserve, could return in Week 7Demarcus Robinson, ankle: Injured reserve, unlikely to play in Week 7De'Zhaun Stribling, ankle: Injured reserve, could return in second half of seasonRicky Pearsall, knee: Out for seasonThe rash of injuries, amazingly, did not slow the 49ers down in their perfect start to the season. But if Evans joins the laundry list of unavailable receivers for any period of time, there is a chance the offense will look more like it did in the second half on Monday than how it appeared over the rest of its first six games.

body:
The two No. 1 seeds in baseball will face off in the World Series, opening in Milwaukee on Friday

        The 2026 World Series matchup is set and the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays will open the Fall Classic at American Family Field on Friday night. The Brewers, fresh off an NLCS sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers, have been resting up since Thursday. The Rays, meanwhile, took six games to take down the Cleveland Guardians and will only have three days off before Game 1.This is a meeting of the two No. 1 seeds in baseball, owners of the best regular-season records in their respective leagues, which happens less often than you'd think in MLB; this is only the sixth time in the Wild Card Era. It's also two franchises that have never won a World Series, meaning we're guaranteed a first-time champion regardless of the outcome.That outcome, you ask? It'll be the end of a hard-fought battle between two similar teams, built around strong pitching (Jacob Misiorowski and Drew Rasmussen, among them) and small ball. The Brewers have more depth in the lineup; the Rays have more power. Milwaukee has a better bullpen.Who wins is up to the players and kind of the managers, depending on who you ask. As for your CBS Sports MLB experts, the best we can do is predict the results.2026 World Series predictions
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Mike Axisa
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Kate Feldman
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Julian McWilliams
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Dayn Perry
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Matt Snyder
                            
            
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Brewers
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Rays
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Brewers
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Brewers
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Brewers
                    
    
    Mike Axisa: I am very much looking forward to this series. I love the style these two teams play. Lots of contact, lots of stolen bases, some power throughout both lineups. Also great pitching. I think the Brewers are just a tiny bit better though, and maybe more than a tiny bit better if Jacob Misiorowski looks like regular-season Misiorowski and not the guy who labored in the NLDS and NLCS. Milwaukee has more depth through the bottom of the lineup and certainly in the bullpen. That's the separator for me. It's been a struggle for Rays manager Kevin Cash to bridge the gap between starter and closer Bryan Baker this postseason. Brewers manager Pat Murphy is loaded with high-end bullpen options. Pick: Brewers in 6
Kate Feldman: So many people are focused on this World Series missing out on the big-name teams, either as a criticism (or defense) of the salary cap or simply because they're Yankees fans, but this is going to be an incredible series. These are the two best teams in baseball and they play a really, really fun game. This is not -- NOT -- anti-home run, but small ball is way more exciting when it's triples and stolen bases like it is with both of these teams rather than sacrifice flies. You're really telling me you don't enjoy watching Chandler Simpson cause chaos on the basepaths? Anyway, I think these two are pretty close to evenly matched and I think the Rays heating up late in the ALCS is going to give them a slight upper hand. But only slight. This is going to be thrilling. Pick: Rays in 7Julian McWilliams: Similar to how I viewed the Guardians against Tampa Bay, I just think Milwaukee is the better overall team. They won 103 games, got through the Dodgers, and have shown all season why they belong on this stage. I respect what the Rays have done, and they're good enough to take a couple games. But when I look at these two teams top to bottom, I trust Milwaukee more. Pick: Brewers in 6Dayn Perry: The Brewers are the better team overall but not by a huge margin, as the Rays are of course the top seed on the AL side. I expect the abundance of rest will help Jacob Misiorowski, who hasn't quite been his usual dominant self in recent starts. That would be a huge boon to Milwaukee's hopes, as they're thin in the rotation right now. The biggest difference for me is the quality of the bullpens. This is a big edge for the Brewers, and I think it'll make the difference in what's going to be a thriller of a series. Pick: Brewers in 7
Matt Snyder: I know that there will be plenty of talk about salaries and markets here, but these are two heavyweights and I'm expecting a lot of back-and-forth uppercuts. Just look at the LCS. The Brewers came from behind every game. The Rays' power started to show up late in the ALCS, and how about the timely insurance home runs from Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz?? We're in for some great pitching matchups, too, with Drew Rasmussen, Freddy Peralta (did you hear he's a former Brewer?), Nick Martinez, Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson. Anyway, it comes down to this for me: The Brewers have been the best team in baseball all season. It's as simple as that. Pick: Brewers in 7

title: Golf rankings: Tom Kim, Shane Lowry move into The Power 18 after worldwide wins - CBS Sports
description: Big names have made their mark on 2026 thanks to wins over
body:
Big names have made their mark on 2026 thanks to wins over the last month
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:55 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                CBS Sports design
            
            

    
        For a golf offseason, there has not been much off about it. In the month since the PGA Tour season wrapped up, the following players have made their way into the winner's circle around the world: Shane Lowry, J.J. Spaun, Matt Fitzpatrick, Tom Kim and Jacob Bridgeman.That is before considering the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club, the marquee event in this portion of the calendar. With big names continuing to play well and big tournaments having transpired and still in the pipeline for the DP World Tour and PGA Tour, golf has continued to showcase the skill and quality of many of the world's best.When that is mentioned, of course, world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler has to be involved. Although the American compiled a 3-1-0 record at the Presidents Cup, Scheffler did not sizzle as most are accustomed to given his play on the PGA Tour and in major championships.He is not in jeopardy of losing his top spot in The Power 18 or anything like that, but it is a hole in the résumé that will only be discussed further since there aren't too many others to point. While he did not take full flight, other Americans like Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup did.
The two teamed up effectively, going 2-0-0 in team sessions. They were countered by Si Woo Kim and Tom Kim for the International team; they continued to serve as the catalysts for the black and gold with another stellar performance in the Presidents Cup.All of those players mentioned are on the move as two-time major champion Jon Rahm drops from the rankings entirely for the first time since I have been at the helm. The Spaniard last teed it up at the BMW PGA Championship, where he finished dead last at 11 over after rounds of 78-77.
The Power 18 provides insight into how golfers are currently performing, based on their play in recent events. It is a wider lens than simply what happened at the last tournament, but narrower than the Official World Golf Rankings, which take into account how more than 2,000 golfers perform across an entire season.The Power 18 golf rankings1
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Scottie Scheffler
                    
            
            
        
Took care of his singles match, got a foursomes win and co-led the U.S. team with three points at the Presidents Cup. Scheffler drew some criticism for his play -- since it may not have been as sharp as usual -- but in a volatile, condensed format, anything can happen, and he still came out on top more often than not. He likely won't be seen again until the Hero World Challenge given what he has done historically.      Previous: 12
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Rory McIlroy
                    
            
            
        
Continues to come oh so close to nabbing his second BMW PGA Championship title. He had just moments at Wentworth where he finished runner-up for the fourth time in his career. That is now three top-five finishes in his last five starts stretching back to the FedEx Cup Playoffs for McIlroy as he gears up for the DP World Tour Playoffs.      Previous: 23
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Matt Fitzpatrick
                    
            
            
        
He just keeps on winning. The Englishman has been hard at work since the PGA Tour season ended, and his work was rewarded with a win at the French Open at Le Golf National. That is now four worldwide victories in 2026 and five in less than a year dating back to the DP World Tour Championship.     Previous: 64
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Chris Gotterup
                    
            
            
        
There are decisions to be made after the top three, and for my money, Gotterup slots in right behind them. After a three-win campaign on the PGA Tour, he was sensational at the Presidents Cup where he nabbed three points in his U.S. team debut. Oftentimes, he was the one who was relied upon as his putter heated up at the precise right time when matches were tight.    Previous: 55
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Wyndham Clark
                    
            
            
        
Played better than his record indicated at the Presidents Cup, Clark was on the receiving end of some high-quality play, like in Sunday singles where he fell to Tom Kim. Still, he showed some guts and gumption that the U.S. team needs moving forward, and his ability on the greens is an asset. Three wins, a major championship and a string of consistency have him as a top-five player at the moment.   Previous: 36
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Cameron Young
                    
            
            
        
For two straight team events, Young has shown up with his best golf. The New Yorker grabbed three points along with Scheffler and Gotterup to lead the U.S. team thanks to a performance on the greens that was missing the last couple of months of the season. He once again proved that, when that club cooperates, there aren't too many that can stand in his way.   Previous: 107
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Sam Burns
                    
            
            
        
Thought he would fare better at the Presidents Cup, but it was not meant to be for Burns. He was one of two Americans to lose their Sunday singles match, and his greatest weapon (the putter) oftentimes left him with more questions than answers. The 2026 season as a whole was the best of his career as he transformed into a much more complete player, but the wins have yet to catch up.   Previous: 48
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Si Woo Kim
                    
            
            
        
Another Presidents Cup and another winning record for Kim, who started 3-0-0 on the week before dropping matches in the final two sessions. Kim may have run out of steam in Chicago, but he was the engine that kept the International team in the fight. The performance came on the heels of the best season of his career, as he continues to gain confidence in the spotlight.   Previous: 89
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Collin Morikawa
                    
            
            
        
Morikawa is a name to circle moving forward given his high level of play while healthy in 2026. Outside of the middle stretch of the year when he struggled to walk, the two-time major champion was as consistent as they come with his putter starting to look much more like an asset towards the end of the year. His health is a question mark, but if it is resolved, he will have everything going his way.   Previous: 1410
    
    
                                            
            
                Ludvig Åberg
            
            
        
Iron play is starting to look like it did early in the year. Åberg connected on a T11 finish at the French Open on the shoulders of his approach numbers and appears primed to get back into the winner's circle over the finishing stretch of this DP World Tour season. The Swede has five top-20 finishes in his last six tournaments.  Previous: 711
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Russell Henley
                    
            
            
        
Didn't have his best Presidents Cup, but that can't drag a player down too far. Henley finished his 2026 season on a high note, all things considered. A win in the middle of the season started a strong run of play through the finish line. In total, he had 12 top-20 finishes in 20 starts and had his best putting season in over a decade.   Previous: 912
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Xander Schauffele
                    
            
            
        
There is a lot to like in the trajectory of Schauffele's game. As sturdy as they come, the two-time major champion finally started to make some putts late in the season to go along with a strong ball-striking campaign. The results followed. Schuaffele took care of Ryan Fox in the anchor match in Sunday singles to improve his record to 12-6-0 in the competition.  Previous: 1213
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Patrick Cantlay
                    
            
            
        
Lost strokes on the greens for only the second time in his PGA Tour career, but Cantlay still showed up come the postseason. His ball striking elevated to new heights, and the Presidents Cup arena proved to be the catalyst for his putting woes. He has been a bright spot for the U.S. team in these events, but the putter needs to get more consistent to get more looks in that format and get back into the winner's circle, where he has not made a trip since 2022.   Previous: 1514
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Tommy Fleetwood
                    
            
            
        
A final-round 64 at the Old Course was enough to catapult Fleetwood's name inside the top five by week's end at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship. Numbers continue to paint a pretty picture, and rounds like that help, but it has been close to one year since the Englishman seriously contended in a tournament. He served as the defending champion when the DP World Tour returned to India and responded with a T5 finish.  Previous: 1115
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Jacob Bridgeman
                    
            
            
        
Didn't get a fair shake in his Presidents Cup debut, but still grabbed the winning point on Sunday when it was all said and done. Bridgeman fired a final-round 61 to win the first event of the FedEx Cup Fall to become the latest multiple-time winner on the PGA Tour this season. He now has three top-10 finishes in a row stretching back to the postseason thanks to rejuvenated iron play.   Previous: Not ranked16
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Tom Kim
                    
            
            
        
Confirmed he is one of those players who rises to the moment in the team events. Kim went a stellar 4-1-0 to lead all points scorers at the Presidents Cup as he took care of Clark in Sunday singles in one of the more anticipated matches. He followed it up by winning the gold medal at the Asian Games, earning an exemption from mandatory military service in South Korea. That counted as his second worldwide win in his last eight tournaments.  Previous: Not ranked17
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                Shane Lowry
                    
            
            
        
Lowry was without a top-20 finish since the Cognizant Classic until he broke the dam at the Irish Open. He ran away and hid with his home country's national open as he finished the week by carding the lowest score in each of the final three rounds to post 23 under and win by 11 strokes. The victory was his first individual title in four years. Previous: Not ranked18
    
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
    
            
    
                    
                J.J. Spaun
                    
            
            
        
Snub season always has a way of producing winners, and this year's winner was Spaun. The former U.S. Open winner became the third American to win the BMW PGA Championship as he outlasted the likes of McIlroy and Adam Scott at Wentworth in his debut appearance. In his last 16 starts, he has two wins and seven other top-25 finishes. Previous: Not ranked

        For the 24th time since the Octagon first touched down in 2010, UFC will promote an event in the city of Abu Dhabi on Saturday as UFC 333 emanates from Etihad Arena in the U.A.E.A pair of title bouts will top the marquee, including a featherweight title showdown in the main event as Alexander Volkanovski looks for the second defense of his second title reign when he welcomes unbeaten Movsar Evloev. In the co-headliner, Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili meet for a third time as Yan sets to defend his bantamweight title after regaining it in December. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 333 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!As we draw closer to this weekend's numbered event, let's take a look at the biggest storylines surrounding UFC 333. 1. Let us never cease to appreciate Alexander "The Great" VolkanovskiOne month after his 38th birthday, the Australian legend remains one of the sport's pound-for-pound best as he looks to pass featherweight legend Jose Aldo's record for the most title wins (while equaling his title defense total) in 145-pound history. Volkanovski, who enters the second title defense of his second reign, has already authored one of the greatest and most successful careers in MMA history after winning his first 12 walks to the Octagon and scoring resounding wins over Chad Mendes, Aldo, Max Holloway (three times), Brian Ortega, Yair Rodriguez and Diego Lopes (twice). But it's his overall longevity and the manner in which he bounced back from consecutive knockout losses to pound-for-pound greats Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria in recent years, only to regain the featherweight crown, that have raised his legend to another level. Volkanovski's meeting with the 20-0 Evloev is basically a betting pick 'em and it's uncertain how much longer the former 214-pound rugby league player can remain atop the featherweight throne. But it remains a joy to watch Volkanovski, who just so happens to have a key acting role in the "Street Fighter" movie that's currently in theaters, and continues to redefine what a fighter in the lower weight divisions can do after turning 35 thanks to his footwork, IQ and adaptability. 
2. Movsar Evloev took the long road to the top of the featherweight divisionThe path to a title shot at the highest levels of the sport of MMA is anything but an exact science and can vary from fighter to fighter depending upon their marketability, fighting style or the depth of their division. For every Josh Hokit, who will compete for the UFC heavyweight title in November just three years after turning pro, there's Evloev, who after 12 years and 20 pro fights will finally get a chance at fulfilling his dream of becoming champion. With a record of 20-0, including wins in all 10 UFC fights dating back to his 2019 debut, Evloev's journey is atypical because of how long he has had to wait. Injuries, illnesses and canceled fights have also been part of the delay for the 32-year-old native of Russia. But even after consecutive wins over Dan Ige, Diego Lopes, Arnold Allen and former 135-pound champion Aljamain Sterling, Evloev still had to wait and watch Lopes fight for the title twice before he ever received his call. Evloev also needed one more victory to secure his spot, which came in March against fellow unbeaten Lerone Murphy -- in his opponent's backyard of London, no less -- when the grappling-heavy Evloev fought back against criticism that he's too boring by striking with Murphy in an exciting majority decision win. Evloev's patience has paid off. And the time spent enduring has also made him a better fighter. And by the way, Evloev's discipline has become so legendary that he has sworn off refined sugars of any kind for a span that has now reached three full years and won't end until he finally wears UFC gold.
3. Petr Yan 2.0 is a scary proposition at bantamweightRaise your hand if you gave up in 2023, when Yan suffered his third consecutive defeat in a decision loss to Dvalishvili, on the idea that the Russian-born former champion was still a threat to the 135-pound title? Sadly, most of us did, too. After a 15-1 start to his career, which included a fifth-round TKO win over Aldo in 2020 to win the vacant UFC bantamweight title, Yan looked like the long-term future of the division thanks to his well-rounded skill set and defiant mean streak. But in hindsight, the four losses he would suffer over his next five fights, with each one coming against elite competition, were a bit deceptive. Yan, now 33, lost his title to Sterling by disqualification in a fight he was winning. He then lost both the rematch and a fight against Sean O'Malley via split decision before taking the first meeting against Dvalishvili with an injured right hand. But after taking a full year off to heal, Yan has returned a determined force. His current four-fight win streak, which includes an upset of Dvalishvili in December to regain the title, has seen him raise his game considerably. In Yan's 2023 loss to "The Machine," he was taken down 11 times by Dvalishvili and only recorded one takedown of his own. That number swung to five takedowns for Yan in the rematch (the most Dvalishvili has yielded in a UFC bout) to just two for Merab, both of which saw Yan quickly return to his feet. Now a two-time champion, Yan is older, wiser and more battle-tested than ever before as he enters the trilogy bout as the betting favorite. 
4. Does Merab Dvalishvili have enough offensive weapons to regain the title? This is a question that few of us saw coming in 2025, when Dvalishvili extended his incredible win streak to 14 fights as he aimed to set a UFC record by defending a title four times in a calendar year. Dvalishvili, who took the Yan rematch just two months after he broke another UFC record by recording 20 takedowns in a decision win over Cory Sandhagen, said he doesn't regret being so ambitious, even if it led to him losing his title. But the bigger question facing him in Saturday's trilogy bout is whether his style was completely solved by Yan in December. Dvalishvili had built so much of his success upon his other-worldly cardio and his relentless ability to spam takedowns in order to control the terms of his fights. Yes, Dvalishvili also improved his striking along the way, which was evidenced in a 2022 win over Aldo in which all 16 of his takedown attempts were stuffed by the Brazilian legend. But his rematch with Yan showed what could happen if someone could both neutralize Dvalishvili's ground attack and prove they could hang with him in terms of pace and aggression. Once that was established, the difference in striking between the two fighters became the story of the fight. And even though Dvalishvili enters their trilogy following a 10-month layoff, which is atypical for someone as active as he normally is, the jury remains out as to whether he can bring enough offensive variety and threat to commandeer his title back from Yan and officially win their rivalry. 
5. Alexander Volkov's heavyweight title hopes likely rest upon a win over Rizvan KunievIn the moments after Volkov lost a highly disputed split decision to Ciryl Gane in their December 2024 rematch, in a fight that almost no one believed Gane had won, UFC CEO and president Dana White could be heard on camera telling the 6-foot-7 Russian that the promotion would make it up to him. A little less than two years later, Gane is booked to make his first heavyweight title defense against the upstart Hokit at UFC 334 in November, which caused the normally mild-mannered Volkov to speak out a bit publicly about his belief that he was passed over. The 2024 Gane rematch remains Volkov's lone defeat in his last seven fights and he has remained perfect since that point, scoring consecutive decision wins over Jailton Almeida and Waldo Cortes-Acosta. But the larger turmoil surrounding the heavyweight division, which included both Jon Jones and Tom Aspinall vacating the title amid former two-division champion Alex Pereira moving up in weight, kept getting in the way of Volkov's hopes and plans. But Volkov, who turns 38 on Saturday, finds himself in a position as a slight betting favorite against countryman Rizvan Kuniev, where his future is likely in his own hands. An impressive victory could make Volkov undeniable for the shot at the winner of Gane-Hokit.

title: Giants release Najee Harris days after criticizing New York's running back rotation - CBS Sports
description: The move comes right after the veteran voiced frustration over his limited role and a crowded backfield rotation
body:
The move comes right after the veteran voiced frustration over his limited role and a crowded backfield rotation in Week 6
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:30 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Giants' running back room and rushing rotation remain in flux, and they have just booted the back who started Sunday's game from the team. The Giants are reportedly releasing Najee Harris, per NFL Media.Harris signed with the Giants in August, and rushed 31 times for 99 yards in five games played. He received the "start" for New York's Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints, but rushed just four times for two yards.Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who entered the game in the fourth quarter, ended up leading the Giants in rushing with 26 yards on just two attempts. Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed six times for 18 yards and a touchdown, Devin Singletary rushed four times for 14 yards and Cam Skattebo was not given a rushing attempt. Harris criticized the Giants' running back rotation after the game on Sunday, saying it was difficult for anyone to find a rhythm. 
"It's hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays," Harris said, via The Trentonian. "The first couple runs will be like, 'OK, how are they playing it?' And then the next ones will be, 'OK, this is how you attack it.' But if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do. That's why I'm saying, 'I don't know.' I've never been through none of this before."Harbaugh was asked by reporters on Monday if he understood why Harris was frustrated with the rotation. The coach said he understood the frustration and respected it, but then explained that playing time had to be earned. "I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities and you're sure to get more opportunities. You know? Do something."
The Giants are likely to add another running back in the near future, but perhaps Harbaugh goes back to Skattebo in Week 7 against the Houston Texans. Skattebo, who lost a key fumble in overtime of the eventual Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders, played just six snaps this past Sunday and did not receive any touches. He is the Giants' leading rusher on the season with 294 yards and one touchdown on 81 carries."I didn't expect to have zero," Skattebo said after the Saints game, via The Athletic. "I was expecting to not play as much just like I did. The message was to keep your head down and keep going. They understand the type of player I am, and I just got to continue doing my job and do it to the best of my ability."Despite the uncertainty at running back, the Giants lead the NFC East at 3-2-1.

        The third season of TGL will feature more players and more teams than any prior iteration of the simulator golf league started by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy. The league founders are both back for the third campaign, and their respective teams will both look different as TGL welcomes an influx of young talent while watching some of the league's seasoned veterans walk away.Originally rostering four players and putting three players in the lineup for each match, TGL teams will now carry five players throughout the 2027 season. Jupiter's Kevin Kisner, New York's Xander Schauffele, Boston's Adam Scott and Atlanta's Lucas Glover are the four former participants who will no longer play in TGL.In their place, young guns like Michael Brennan, Ben James, Blades Brown and Jackson Koivun will tee it up at the SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. Koivun was announced as a member of Brooks Koepka's Motor City Golf Club a couple of weeks ago as a part of the league's first expansion team.

description: The veteran defensive tackle appeared in all five games this season after following head coach Robert Saleh to Te
body:
The veteran defensive tackle appeared in all five games this season after following head coach Robert Saleh to Tennessee from San Francisco
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:47 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Tennessee Titans earned their first win of the 2026 season and of the Robert Saleh era this past Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts, upsetting their rivals in Indy, 26-20. However, they were forced to release one of their defensive linemen this week after an "incident" at the team facility. On Tuesday, the team announced that it had released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after reviewing an incident that happened on Thursday. The Titans issued a statement through team reporter Jim Wyatt. "On Thursday, Oct. 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott.Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter."It's unclear what the incident was or if any more information will come out about it. Elliott has played in all five games this season with one start and has recorded 11 tackles. He followed Saleh over from the San Francisco 49ers, as Elliott spent the past two seasons out in Santa Clara, making 29 starts in 31 games played. 
Elliott's surprising release is not the only strange occurrence the Titans are dealing with, as the team also made starting cornerback and $58 million free-agent addition Alontae Taylor inactive in Week 6. They didn't just bench him; they took his uniform away. It was described as a coach's decision, and Saleh has refused to elaborate on the situation. "We'll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best for the team moving forward," Saleh told reporters on Monday. 
The Titans return home this week to host the 4-2 Cleveland Browns, who currently lead the AFC North.

title: How the Brewers could join elite company with World Series title after dominant regular season - CBS Sports
description: Milwaukee is just four wins away from the first ring in franchise history, fresh off MLB's best regular-season re
body:
Milwaukee is just four wins away from the first ring in franchise history, fresh off MLB's best regular-season record
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Milwaukee Brewers are four wins away from the first World Series title in franchise history. Given that they're the superior team in their matchup with the Tampa Bay Rays and much more rested, the expectation in most quarters is that they'll get those four wins. That alone is special enough – the whole point, you would agree. The Brewers, though, are also four wins away from joining an even more exclusive cohort of World Series champions: those teams that not only won the World Series but did so after dominating the regular season. Especially in this ongoing era of playoff bloat, Major League Baseball more often than not awards the belt and the title to a team that, from April through September, was something less than the best club. That's the nature of the sport when you reduce it to the relatively tiny sample of games found in the postseason, grow the field, and let randomness rule. It's a sport already built upon a certain level of unpredictability. For instance, the 2017 Dodgers -- en route to winning 104 games and the pennant -- lost 16 of 17 at one point. The 2006 Cardinals eked out 83 wins in the regular season before barging to the championship in October. The 1988 Mets went 10-1 against the Dodgers in the regular season but then fell to them in seven games in the NLCS. These, of course, are just a handful of the many examples.The upshot of all this is that in MLB, the best team during the regular season doesn't wind up hoisting the trophy as often as it does in the NFL, NBA, and NHL. The shame of it is that the 162-game regular season, because of its remorseless breadth and everyday-ness, is a true cauldron and, in an ideal world, the sport's defining feature. Forging the most wins across those six months means something, and indeed by any sensible standard it means more than stacking up 11 or 13 wins in October. If horse sense prevailed, then MLB would reward the team with the best regular season with some kind of hardware that reflects the hard-won nature of the achievement. On this point, please permit the writer to quote the current Collective Bargaining Agreement between players and clubs: 
"During the term of this Agreement, each Club shall be scheduled to play 162 games during each championship season."Emphasis mine, but I'm willing to share it. Yes, the regular season in officially official terms is known as the "championship season." But, to our grave cultural diminishment, we don't really treat it as such. Instead, it's an exercise in qualification and seeding for October. I'm disappointed in all of you for this.In lieu of proper sanctioned recognition for excellence across 162, we turn back to the Brewers and the select company they may soon join. This year's World Series will be the 122nd between National and American League clubs. Of those 121 to date, though, just 29 World Series winners have paired that honor with the best regular-season record and the best regular-season run differential (runs scored minus runs allowed). The current Brewers model, with their MLB-best 103 wins during the championship season and MLB-best +214 run differential, are in position to become the 30th team to claim what we'll hereby call the Team Triple Crown. To restate, a club wins the Team Triple Crown when, in the same year, they win the World Series after achieving the best record and best run differential during the regular season (no ties permitted, which means teams that tied for the best regular-season record or run differential before winning the World Series are not allowed; a Team Triple Crown winner must stand alone on all fronts). 
As for the company Milwaukee may soon keep, here's the current list of MLB Team Triple Crown winners:Team 				Record 				Run Differential 				2024 Los Angeles Dodgers98-64+1562016 Chicago Cubs 				103-58 				+252 				1998 New York Yankees 				114-48 				+309 				1989 Oakland Athletics 				99-63 				+136 				1986 New York Mets 				108-54 				+205 				1984 Detroit Tigers 				104-58 				+186 				1975 Cincinnati Reds 				108-54 				+254 				1970 Baltimore Orioles 				108-54 				+218 				1968 Detroit Tigers 				103-59 				+179 				1967 St. Louis Cardinals 				101-60 				+138 				1961 New York Yankees 				109-53 				+215 				1956 New York Yankees 				97-57 				+226 				1948 Cleveland Indians 				97-58 				+272 				1947 New York Yankees 				97-57 				+226 				1944 St. Louis Cardinals 				105-49 				+282 				1940 Cincinnati Reds 				100-53 				+179 				1939 New York Yankees 				106-45 				+411 				1938 New York Yankees 				99-53 				+256 				1937 New York Yankees 				102-52 				+308 				1936 New York Yankees 				102-51 				+334 				1932 New York Yankees 				107-47 				+278 				1929 Philadelphia Athletics 				104-46 				+286 				1927 New York Yankees 				110-44 				+376 				1923 New York Yankees 				98-54 				+201 				1919 Cincinnati Reds 				96-44 				+176 				1917 Chicago White Sox 				100-54 				+192 				1912 Boston Red Sox 				105-47 				+255 				1907 Chicago Cubs 				107-45 				+184 				1905 New York Giants 				105-48 				+275 				Note: No, the 2020 season, abbreviated to 60 regular season games because of COVID, does not count. If the Brewers are able to pull off the Team Triple Crown, then they'd be just the 30th team ever to do so. As you would expect, the Yankees have easily the most Team Triple Crowns with 12 (out of 27 championships overall). Winning four Team Triple Crowns in a row back in the 1930s is particularly impressive. The colossus in the Bronx back in the day of course turned dominance into tedium. Winning the Team Triple Crown these days is more impressive than it's ever been. We're deep into the expansion era, obviously, and since 1995 there's that third layer of the playoffs that the best teams must fight through. That's why just three squadrons -- the '98 Yankees, the 2016 Cubs, and the 2024 Dodgers -- stand as Team Triple Crown winners since the Division Series was instituted. It's really, really hard to pull it off these days, but the Brewers are tantalizingly close to joining them. For the Brewers, that means a World Series crown, provided it's forthcoming, will have been truly earned in every sense. It's already been a season to remember in Milwaukee, and they're close to joining company that's even more exclusive than you might think.

title: Jalen Hurts blood clot diagnosis timeline: Where the situation started, how it developed and where it is now - CBS Sports
description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were found in his lungs. S
body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were found in his lungs. Speculation about the injury began shortly after the team announced he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf, which sidelined him for the Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers.The team said his prognosis is "very good," and he is expected to make a full recovery. He's currently on blood thinners, which prevent him from participating in any contact activities until he's fully recovered. The severity of the injury has caused great concern over Hurts' future and has some calling for an investigation into how the Eagles approached the injury and treatment. A lot has transpired in a short amount of time, and the timeline can get a bit confusing. His diagnosis also changed over the course of a week. So let's break it down to the facts:Oct. 4: Eagles vs. RamsThis is the game where Hurts said the blood clot was "provoked." He was cleated in his calf during the 24-20 loss.
Oct. 8: Hurts seeks treatment for calfAfter practice, Hurts sought treatment on his calf, the original spot of the blood clot. Hurts was listed with a calf injury on the Week 5 injury report, but he was a full participant in Friday's practice ahead of the Eagles' trip to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars. Oct. 9: Eagles, Hurts fly to LondonThe team flew to London on the Friday before their international game, arriving late Friday night for the trip across the pond. The team would be in London for less than 48 hours. Hurts flew with the team, and the flight from Philly to London takes between seven and eight hours. Oct. 10: Blood clot reportedly detectedWhile in London, Hurts was seen by specialists, who reportedly found the blood clot through an MRI. According to reports, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 a.m. local time. Initial reports said Hurts was advised by medical professionals not to sleep and had been up 36 hours before taking the field on Sunday. However, the QB's agent, Nicole Lynn, later released a statement saying that although Hurts stayed up late, he managed to get some sleep before the game. She said the team set up a room for him at the stadium.
The Eagles' medical staff and independent doctors told Hurts and the team that "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play," per a statement the team released on Oct. 15.Oct. 11: Eagles vs. Jaguars in LondonHurts played the full game, throwing for 220 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles lost 19-17 and fell to 2-3 on the season. Oct. 11: Eagles fly home from LondonThe Eagles flew home from London the night of the game. Hurts was on the flight, which, again, would have taken between seven and eight hours. 
Oct. 14: Hurts undergoes second ultrasoundHurts was once again listed with a calf injury, this time on the Wednesday, Oct. 14 injury report, but was a full participant. Speaking with the media, before his test, he called his injury a "unique experience."After practice, he underwent a second ultrasound, where doctors found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation. Oct. 15: Hurts misses practice After being a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Hurts was a non-participant in both Thursday and Friday's practices.
Oct. 15: Eagles announce Hurts is outThe team released a statement explaining that Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot when he initially sought treatment. They made the announcement that Hurts would be sidelined for their Week 6 game. 
Oct. 16: Eagles sign Joe MiltonThe Eagles signed quarterback Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad. The move felt like a premonition of Hurts going on IR, due to the number of quarterbacks they were carrying.Oct. 17: Eagles put Hurts on IRShortly after reports that they would not be placing Hurts on IR, the Eagles did, in fact, put the QB on IR. Any player on IR is required to miss a minimum of four games.
Oct. 18: Eagles vs. PanthersHurts was ruled out ahead of the Week 6 contest, and Tanner McKee started in his place. McKee went 26-of-45 with 215 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. The Eagles fell to 2-4 on the season.Oct. 19: Eagles release statementThe Eagles released a statement with an update on the situation. They said Hurts was "initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli." Pulmonary emboli means there were multiple blood clots now in his lungs, which is a serious situation.The team said it expects him to make a full recovery and anticipates "that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners." More reports also came out at this time about Hurts' hospital stay in London and his lack of sleep before the Week 5 game.
Oct. 19: Reports on his season being overOn Monday, there were multiple reports that Hurts' season was likely over, given his situation. While it seems likely, there has been no confirmation from the Eagles on an official timetable or return plan.

title: ACC midseason grades: Miami posts an 'A,' Florida State and Clemson earn 'Ds' - CBS Sports
description: As we hit the midseason checkpoint of the 2026 college football schedule, the ACC finds itself very much in the national title race but
body:
As we hit the midseason checkpoint of the 2026 college football schedule, the ACC finds itself very much in the national title race but also falling short too often against its peers. The league holds a 6-11 record against other power-conference opponents (plus Notre Dame) and has just one team in the current AP Top 25. It's just that team happens to be No. 1 in the country and currently sits as a consensus top-four pick to win the national championship in the eyes of the oddsmakers. Yes, Miami's success does count as the ACC's success when we look at how the league is performing overall so far this season. The Hurricanes have met expectations at nearly every turn after finishing last year as the national runner-up, and after a 6-0 start, the ability to close strong and win the conference for the first time ever will become a prominent storyline within the league. But the league also gets to boast about the success story of Wake Forest, which has raced out to a 5-1 start, with its only loss a 13-point defeat to the Miami Hurricanes. While Miami has met expectations, Wake Forest has more than exceeded them, and now the conversations around Winston-Salem are about how close the Demon Deacons could be to recording a truly banner year for the program. 
Those success stories have earned the best grades in our assessment of all 17 ACC teams, which, on the whole, included few honor roll candidates. There are multiple hot-seat situations, some Year 1 hires off to rough starts, and more than a handful of frustrating losses in that 6-11 record against other power-conference teams. As a connoisseur of academic eligibility, I can confirm that C's do indeed earn degrees, but graduation is not the goal in many of these programs.
        
            
                2026 CBS Sports Midseason All-America team: Big Ten edges out SEC, ACC for most selections at halfway point
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Boston CollegeRecord: 3-3, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A Saturday's home win at Pitt meant a lot to Boston College because it backed up a couple of weeks of improved play with a positive result. After enduring an absolute slop-fest in the rain and losing 21-14 to Virginia Tech, the Eagles fought hard but were ultimately out-manned in a 25-16 loss at SMU. You could sense that the team, improved on defense and figuring it out with dual-threat quarterback Mason McKenzie, was getting better, but it was storming back from a 12-0 deficit to beat the Panthers that gives a much more positive spin to the team's midseason grade. Grade: C- 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    CaliforniaRecord: 3-4, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A The inconsistency coming out of Cal can be dizzying, as the program has been changing quarterbacks and play-callers while trying to find answers to problems that are causing the Bears to fall short of expectations. At 3-4 overall, there's still a path to bowl eligibility in Year 1 of the Tosh Lupoi era, but it will likely require more steps forward for an offense that is averaging just 19.7 points per game against FBS opponents (106th nationally). Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has dealt with injury issues, and the run game has been stuck in the mud, leaving a lot to work on when Cal finally hits its off week on Nov. 7. Grade: D   

                            
    
                                                
                    
    ClemsonRecord: 4-2, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AWe can't technically prove it, but this feels like the lowest grade possible for a team that's still very much alive in the conference title race. Clemson is 4-2 overall and 2-1 in ACC play, and the Tigers have already faced a lot of the tougher opponents on their schedule. But the quality of the performance has been far below the typical expectations for Clemson football. Among ACC teams, the Tigers have been a bottom-five offense and fairly middling on defense, with quarterback play that has produced two passing touchdowns to five interceptions between Tait Reynolds and Chris Vizzina. That hasn't been anywhere near the standard of a program looking to win the league for a third time in five years. Grade: D 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Duke    Record: 4-2, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A  You hate seeing back-to-back losses after a 4-0 start, and it's especially frustrating to drop those games in conference play after winning the ACC Championship in 2025. Unfortunately for Duke, the schedule only gets tougher coming down the stretch with games against Miami, Clemson and Wake Forest in successive weeks to close the regular season, and currently this team's best win was beating Illinois back on Sept. 12. The Blue Devils have been able to circle the wagons before after some midseason setbacks, but this will be a daunting challenge for the reigning league champs. Grade: C+   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida State  Record: 3-4, 1-3 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A If this were Year 1 of the Mike Norvell era, we could highlight the competitiveness in close losses to Miami and SMU, or the way he had the team prepared to punch first in a tough road spot at Alabama. But close only counts with horseshoes and hand grenades, and certainly not in a hot-seat season at a program with three national championships in the last 30 years. The Seminoles were alarmingly non-competitive in the second half of a road loss at Louisville, and after the crushing loss to rival Miami, now sit tied for 15th in the ACC standings. That's unacceptable for Florida State football and certainly not a marker of success midway through Norvell's seventh season with the program. Grade: D 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Georgia TechRecord: 2-4, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AIt's a good thing that Georgia Tech knocked off Duke in Week 6 and backed it up with a better effort in a loss to Virginia Tech, because the Yellow Jackets were trending toward having one of the worst midseason grades in the ACC. And while we have kept this space mostly free from the odds market, it is sometimes informative to judge teams with an eye on their performance in relation to the point spread. To that point, Georgia Tech has been as bad as they come, going 1-5 against the spread and failing to cover the oddsmaker's number by an average of 4.08 points per game (112th nationally). It's a team that has not been meeting expectations in the big picture or on a week-to-week basis, and that's going to get a grade that's barely passable. Grade: D  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Louisville Record: 4-3, 3-2 | Preseason AP ranking: 24 Are the vibes around the Cards better now? When Louisville was 2-3 and fumbling the game away in Raleigh, it seemed like the sky was falling, but after throttling Florida State and surviving at Syracuse, this year's group seems to have found their footing. Louisville has two conference losses, but the head-to-head advantage against SMU keeps them alive for the conference championship game, with a favorable remaining league schedule. The Cards are off in Week 8 but will return to action with games against Stanford and Georgia Tech. Win those both, and a shot at the conference title is on the line coming down the stretch. Grade: C+  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Miami Record: 6-0, 4-0 | Preseason AP ranking: 7Mario Cristobal took two years to lay the foundation, but it's clear that all the visions of re-establishing The U as a national power in college football were not delusions. This week, Miami returned to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll for the first time since 2002, hitting yet another benchmark for excellence in meeting the program's historic standard. Miami is 6-0 and currently leads the ACC in scoring offense, total offense, scoring defense and total defense, with those offensive numbers ranking among the best in the country. So yes, the Hurricanes are rolling and very much the class of the conference, even as they continue to pursue the program's first ACC title since joining the league in 2004. Grade: A 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    NC State Record: 3-3, 1-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A The Wolfpack's midseason grade was actually saved here by the way the team broke out from the frustration of fourth-quarter failures to take down Louisville earlier this month. That's a good win for anyone, but it was much needed given the team's performance and results through the first four games of the year. Unfortunately, the positivity gained from that win seemed to get reset a bit when Wake Forest ran away with a 24-point win in Raleigh the next week. The team is 3-3 overall but has some favorable opportunities ahead with games against Stanford and Cal, so these next couple of weeks could tell us a lot about the ability for Dave Doeren's crew to close the year strong. Grade: C-   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    North Carolina Record: 4-2, 2-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A The best thing that North Carolina has going for it is a very clear sense of identity, and that confidence has powered three close wins against power conference teams in the first half of the season. The Tar Heels are one of the least-penalized teams in the country (top-10 in both penalties per game and penalty yards per game), and the defense has come up with game-changing stops in clutch situations in each of its last two ACC wins. North Carolina's offensive ceiling is not instilling fear in opponents (99th nationally in scoring offense at 23.5 points per game), but Year 2 of the Bill Belichick era has produced a gritty group that will drag you into the mud and test your execution in close, late-game situations. Grade: B-  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    PittsburghRecord: 5-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A It's incredibly unsettling how quickly things have seemed to spiral for Pitt after racing out to a 5-0 start with a roar of a win against Virginia Tech in Blacksburg. But the Panthers are 0-2 since and just got outplayed by Boston College in a 27-21 loss up in Chestnut Hill, meaning the impact of Mason Heinstschel's season-ending knee injury might be even greater than we imagined at the time. There is still a lot of season left to rally and log a couple of quality wins for the campaign, but the team that finishes the second half of the season won't be expected to win at the same clip. Grade: B- 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 23 SMURecord: 5-1, 3-1 | Preseason AP ranking: 19It's been an odd, somewhat disjointed season for SMU: the Mustangs have never fallen out of contention for any of their goals, yet have yet to register a statement win. Rhett Lashlee's crew will have those opportunities next month with a visit from Wake Forest and a trip to Notre Dame, but for now SMU has been quietly handling its business and winning the games it should win ever since a tough 41-31 loss at Louisville back in Week 3. There's plenty to clean up at the margins with their performance, but ultimately SMU is still on track to meet expectations. Grade: B 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Stanford Record: 3-4, 1-3 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A It brings me no joy to give a failing grade to one of our nation's elite institutions, but there's some work to be done before finals if we're going to come out of the 2026 season with a passing grade. Tavita Pritchard has a group that is 1-4 against power-conference opponents and ranks 133rd nationally in scoring margin (-18.3 points per game). Outside of a 34-27 home win against Georgia Tech back on Sept. 26, there haven't been a lot of encouraging signs for closing the gap with the rest of the conference. Grade F    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Syracuse Record: 2-4, 0-4 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AIt is not wrong to point out that Syracuse is a few plays away from being a 5-1 football team. Close losses to Cal, Virginia and Louisville all have "what if" moments that have left Orange fans feeling frustrated about the potential for a second straight season of sub-.500 results. The football itself has been pretty competitive and impressive for how the offense has endured an absolute carousel at quarterback, but a -5 turnover margin in conference play has been among the many reasons the Orange keep winding up losing these close games. Grade: C- 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    VirginiaRecord: 4-3, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/AIn terms of quality, there is a nagging concern that Virginia played its best game of the season in Week 0 against NC State. The Wahoos were the better-prepared team, seemed to be clicking on all cylinders with new starting quarterback Beau Pribula and cruised to a 34-8 win that seemed even more lopsided than the final score. But since then, Virginia is 1-3 against power-conference opponents; the closest the team has come to recapturing that Week 0 form was a 42-3 win over Delaware. There seems to be a high floor here that sets up for Virginia to be competitive in most games the rest of the way, but hopes of a return to the ACC title game look less likely here at the midseason checkpoint. Grade: C 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Virginia TechRecord: 5-2, 2-2 | Preseason AP ranking: N/ASaturday's game at Death Valley is a measuring stick moment for Virginia Tech football in Year 1 under James Franklin. And if the Hokies can go get a win, this might jump up a letter grade. With a 5-2 record through seven games, the Hokies are pacing toward an 8-4 finish that meets most reasonable expectations for Franklin's first season in Blacksburg. They survived the double heartbreak of a missed kick to win against Pitt and the ensuing nightmare trip to Cal to find themselves right on the doorstep of a couple of statement win opportunities. This Virginia Tech team is about to play road games at Clemson, SMU and Miami in the next five weeks, and how the Hokies perform will give us a great idea of where the program currently sits in the ACC hierarchy. Grade: B- 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 17 Wake ForestRecord: 6-1, 4-1 | Preseason AP ranking: N/A Jake Dickert likes to say Wake Forest was built in the darkness, but his work with the Demon Deacons' success is worth the spotlight. Gio Lopez has been stellar with 17 touchdowns and just one interception, while Carlos Hernandez's development has continued to the point where he's one of the most productive receivers in the ACC. All of it has set up Wake Forest to have a top-three scoring offense in the league (37.4 points per game) and an inside track to contend for a spot in the ACC Championship Game. Grade: A

The Buckeyes face a complicated path in the wake of Sayin's injury, while Miami takes over the No. 1 seed in our latest projection
